f.modes.keys: `i a I A o O Esc`
f.modes.what: enter insert at cursor / after / line start / line end / new line below / above

f.xdd.what: delete char, delete line, yank line, paste after/before

m.word.what: next word start, prev word start, word end, prev word end

m.line.what: line start, first non-blank, line end

m.find.what: jump to / till a character forward or back, on the current line

m.repeatfind.what: repeat last f/t forward or back

m.screenpos.what: cursor to screen top/middle/bottom; scroll line to centre/top/bottom

o.change.what: delete then insert; `C` to end of line; `s` one char

o.replace.what: replace one char / enter replace mode

o.filter.what: pipe lines through a shell command

v.blockedit.what: insert/append/change on every line of a block

v.reselect.what: reselect last visual; swap selection end

r.named.what: yank/put to a named register; uppercase appends

x.lastsearch.what: reuse the search pattern; change-next-match repeatable

x.global.what: run a command on matching lines

x.normal.what: run normal-mode keys over a range

x.cmdline.what: insert word under cursor, command history, repeat last Ex

a.macroedit.what: paste, fix and re-yank a macro

a.recursive.what: recursive macro to end of file

n.marks.what: set / jump to a mark (line / exact)

n.autmarks.what: last jump, last change, last insert

n.folds.keys: `zo zc za zR zM zj zk`

i.delete.what: delete word / to line start / char without leaving insert

i.oneshot.what: run one normal command, stay in insert

i.escape.what: leave insert without reaching for Esc

w.move.keys: `Ctrl-w h j k l w p c o`

nv.lsp.keys: `grn gra grr gri gd K Ctrl-]`

nv.treesitter.keys: `af if ac ic` via mini.ai / textobjects

tips.f.modes: Use `A` to append at the end of a line and `O` to open a line above, instead of moving first and then pressing `i`.
tips.f.undo: After an undo, `Ctrl-r` redoes it; you never need to retype what you just undid.
tips.m.word: Reach for `w`, `b` and `e` before holding `l`: one key per word instead of one per character.
tips.m.WORD: `W` and `B` skip over punctuation like `foo.bar(baz)` in one hop.
tips.m.line: `^` lands on the first non-blank character, which is where you usually want to be in indented code.
tips.m.find: `f(` jumps straight to the opening parenthesis of a call on the current line.
tips.m.repeatfind: After `f,`, press `;` to hop to the next comma instead of typing `f,` again.
tips.m.count: Put a count before a motion: `3w` moves three words in two keystrokes.
tips.m.file: `gg` and `G` jump to the start and end of the file; `42G` goes straight to line 42.
tips.m.para: `}` jumps to the next blank line, which in most code means the next function or block.
tips.m.rel: Turn on `relativenumber` and jump to any visible line with `{count}j` or `{count}k`.
tips.m.match: Press `%` on a bracket to jump to its partner, handy for finding the end of a long call.
tips.m.search: `/name<CR>` is often the fastest way to reach a line you cannot see.
tips.m.star: `*` searches for the word under the cursor; then `n` walks through every use.
tips.o.delete: `D` deletes to the end of the line; `dw` and `d$` compose with any motion.
tips.o.change: `cw` replaces a word and leaves you in insert mode, saving a separate `dw` and `i`.
tips.o.yank: `yiw` copies the word under the cursor without moving to its start first.
tips.o.dot: Make an edit once, then press `.` on the next spot: the cheapest repeat in Vim.
tips.o.indent: `>ip` indents the whole paragraph; `=ip` re-indents it.
tips.o.case: `gUiw` uppercases the word under the cursor, great for constants.
tips.o.join: `J` joins the next line onto this one with a single space.
tips.o.number: `Ctrl-a` increments the number under (or after) the cursor; `5Ctrl-a` adds five.
tips.t.word: `ciw` changes the whole word from anywhere inside it.
tips.t.quote: `ci"` changes a string's contents from anywhere inside the quotes.
tips.t.paren: `ci(` rewrites all the arguments of a call in one go.
tips.t.bracket: `di[` empties a list or index expression without touching the brackets.
tips.t.brace: `di{` clears the body of a block or object literal.
tips.t.tag: `cit` changes the text inside an HTML or JSX tag.
tips.t.para: `yap` copies a whole paragraph or function, including the trailing blank line.
tips.t.compose: Think in verb plus noun: `da(`, `yi"`, `>ip` all work the same way.
tips.v.line: `V` then `j`/`k` selects whole lines; `>` indents the selection.
tips.v.block: `Ctrl-v` selects a column; it is Vim's native multi-cursor.
tips.v.blockedit: `Ctrl-v`, select lines, `$A;<Esc>` appends a semicolon to every line.
tips.v.reselect: `gv` reselects the last visual selection, so you can apply a second operator.
tips.r.named: `"ayy` yanks into register a; `"ap` pastes it back even after other yanks.
tips.r.yank0: `"0p` pastes what you last yanked, even after `dd` overwrote the default register.
tips.r.insert: In insert mode, `Ctrl-r 0` pastes your last yank without leaving insert.
tips.x.subst: `:%s/old/new/g` renames every occurrence in the file at once.
tips.x.lastsearch: Search with `/foo`, then `cgn` and `.` to change matches one at a time.
tips.x.global: `:g/pattern/d` deletes every line that matches, in one command.
tips.x.normal: `:'<,'>normal A;` appends a semicolon to every selected line.
tips.x.copymove: `:m+1` moves the current line down one; `:t.` duplicates it.
tips.a.dot: Design edits to be repeatable: `A;<Esc>` then `j.` beats editing each line by hand.
tips.a.macro: Record with `qa`, stop with `q`, replay with `@a`, then `@@` to repeat.
tips.n.marks: `ma` sets a mark; `'a` jumps back to that line from anywhere in the file.
tips.n.jumplist: `Ctrl-o` takes you back to where you were before a jump or search.
tips.n.lastinsert: `gi` resumes inserting exactly where you last left insert mode.
tips.n.unmatched: `[{` jumps to the start of the enclosing block from anywhere inside it.
tips.i.delete: In insert mode, `Ctrl-w` deletes the previous word without leaving insert.
tips.i.oneshot: `Ctrl-o` runs one normal-mode command and drops you back into insert.
tips.i.escape: `Ctrl-[` leaves insert mode without reaching for the Escape key.
tips.nv.comment: `gcc` toggles a comment on the current line; `gcip` comments a paragraph.
